_README: Integration calls the endpoint catalog cannot serve.
IT IS EMPTY, AND MUST STAY EMPTY.
This is a RATCHET, not an exemption list. It is asserted exactly in both
directions: a NEW breach fails CI, and so does a STALE entry, so fixing
one means deleting its line. Adding a line is a decision to ship a test
that cannot fail -- against a live Ghidra every one of these still
returns 200, because AnnotationScanner simply does not find an
undeclared parameter and uses the default instead.
History: the check was written for #467 with ten read-only breaches
already fixed, and immediately found 29 more in the other nine files.
Those were paid off in #475 (2026-08-31). What that pass actually found:
26 were real, and are fixed, redirected or deleted with the missing
capability recorded in the test file itself.
3 were the CHECK'S OWN false positives -- `by_path.get("/set_global")`
is a dict lookup over the endpoint catalog, not a GET, and three of
those were reported as method_not_allowed against POST endpoints no
test ever called with GET. HTTP_RECEIVERS / NON_HTTP_RECEIVERS now
classify every receiver, and an unclassified one fails loudly.
5 more were INVISIBLE to the check and are now covered: four JSON
bodies (`http_client.post` takes `json_data=`, which was missing
from _PARAM_KWARGS) and one f-string URL
(`http_session.get(f"{server_url}/list_functions", ...)`). Two of
the newly visible ones were in tests/conftest.py's SHARED fixtures,
which every test in the tier inherits.
The three shapes, all mechanical to fix:
unknown_parameter   The name is wrong, or the endpoint has no such
parameter at all. /list_functions was the common
one: ListingService documents it as 'List all
functions (no pagination)' and declares only
`program`, so every `limit` sent to it was dropped.
Pagination lives on /list_functions_enhanced and
/search_functions.
method_not_allowed  A POST endpoint called with GET. NOT a 404: the
plugin registers one context per path and does not
enforce the method, so the handler ran with an
EMPTY body and every ParamSource.BODY parameter
resolved to its default. That is why these tests
passed -- they asserted 200 on a stated error.
Correcting one can move a test into a mutating
tier, so check whether the endpoint writes: the
five fixed here (analyze_data_region,
detect_array_bounds, get_assembly_context,
analyze_struct_field_usage,
get_field_access_context) open no transaction and
are POST only because their payloads are
structured.
no_such_endpoint    The route does not exist. PR #459 settled that the
@McpTool annotations are authoritative, so this is
a broken test, not a missing feature. Replacements
used here: /batch_rename_variables ->
/rename_variables; /run_script ->
/run_ghidra_script. /build_function_hash_index and
/lookup_function_by_hash describe a persistent
index and a reverse hash->function lookup that
this server does not have; the surviving surface is
/get_function_hash + /get_bulk_function_hashes.
